title: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3
summary: Specifies TLS version 1.3, providing secure communication over the Internet. It deprecates obsolete cryptographic algorithms (RC4, SHA-1, MD5, static RSA key exchange, CBC-mode ciphers), mandates Forward Secrecy via ECDHE/DHE, encrypts handshake messages including server certificates, and reduces connection setup latency to 1-RTT (with optional 0-RTT resumption).
key_mechanisms: Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) ciphers only (AES-GCM, AES-CCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305)
Zero Round Trip Time (0-RTT) Early Data

title: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.2
summary: Specifies TLS 1.2, replacing MD5/SHA-1 in the PRF with SHA-256 and adding support for Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) ciphers like AES-GCM.
key_mechanisms: Configurable signature and hash algorithm negotiation

title: Security Architecture for the Internet Protocol
summary: Defines the base architecture for IPsec-compliant network layer security. Details the interaction between the Security Policy Database (SPD), Security Association Database (SAD), Peer Authorization Database (PAD), and traffic selectors, providing confidentiality and integrity for IPv4 and IPv6 packets.
key_mechanisms: Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) per RFC 4303 for confidentiality and integrity
Authentication Header (AH) per RFC 4302 for integrity without confidentiality
Security Associations (SA) identified by SPI, IP destination, and protocol

title: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
summary: Comprehensive specification of TCP incorporating four decades of updates. Covers connection establishment (three-way handshake), state machine, sequence number validation to prevent blind spoofing and reset attacks, and window management.
key_mechanisms: Protection against off-path TCP attacks via randomized initial sequence numbers (ISNs)
TIME_WAIT state management and socket lifecycle
TCP SYN Cookie defense against denial-of-service

title: Linux Kernel Netfilter Subsystem Use-After-Free Privilege Escalation
summary: A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel nf_tables subsystem allows a local unprivileged user to escalate privileges to root via crafted batch requests manipulating anonymous sets.

title: Linux Kernel DCCP Socket Double-Free Local Privilege Escalation
summary: A double-free flaw in the Datagram Congestion Control Protocol (DCCP) implementation (IP_PKTOPTIONS / dccp_rcv_state_process) allowed unprivileged local users to overwrite kernel memory and gain root.
mitigations: Disable DCCP module: install dccp /bin/true in modprobe configuration
Kernel patch ensuring skb destruction accounting

title: Linux Socket Security Mechanisms and Hardening Standards
system: Linux Kernel Socket API & POSIX Networking
summary: Essential security options and controls for hardening network sockets in Linux environments.
key_mechanisms: SO_BINDTODEVICE: Restricts socket binding exclusively to a designated network interface, preventing cross-interface packet leaking.
SO_PASSCRED: Enables atomic retrieval of SCM_CREDENTIALS (pid, uid, gid) for peer authentication across UNIX domain sockets.
CAP_NET_RAW / CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE: Linux capabilities required for raw socket access and binding to privileged ports (<1024).
Network Namespaces (CLONE_NEWNET): Complete isolation of network devices, routing tables, and firewall rules.
